sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's >>= operator silently propagates Nothing through an entire chain — once any step yields Nothing, all subsequent steps are skipped without error.
sketches.resonance: Grief works like Nothing: once it enters the chain, everything afterward is quietly hollowed out, and the rest of life still type-checks but never runs.
sketches.draft:
grief :: Maybe a -> Maybe a
grief life = life
  >>= return
  >>= return
  >>= const Nothing
  >>= return
  >>= return
  >>= return

sketches.mechanism: An interface with a single abstract method that can never be satisfied — the return type demands something the parameter cannot provide, making implementation a declaration of intent that cannot execute.
sketches.resonance: A promise is an interface you declare knowing no implementation will ever fulfill it.

sketches.mechanism: A LEFT JOIN where the right table is empty — every row from the left survives but is padded with NULLs, producing results that are structurally complete but substantively hollow.
sketches.resonance: You can join yourself to what is gone and get back every row of your life intact, but every column where they should appear is NULL.
